officials.name: Jim Ross
officials.bio: Mayor Jim Ross was elected to the office of Mayor at the City of Arlington in June 2021. Jim has spent decades serving his community and his country. As a proud resident of Arlington for forty years, he has witnessed the growth and growing pains this community has endured.

officials.name: John Cowen, Jr.
officials.bio: Honorable Mayor John Cowen, Jr. is a distinguished public servant and a 6th generation Brownsvillian. Elected as Mayor in 2023, he leads key initiatives to enhance the city's economy, infrastructure, quality of life, and long-term development.

officials.name: Kevin Webb
officials.bio: Kevin Webb was elected in November of 2012 and has won re-election twice. Born and raised in Comal County, he graduated from New Braunfels High School and Texas A&M with a B.S. in Recreation, Parks, and Tourism. In office, Kevin has primarily focused on transportation and currently serves as the Vice Chairman of the Alamo Area Metropolitan Planning Organization (AAMPO).

officials.name: Dr. Josh Acevedo
officials.bio: Representative Josh Acevedo was born and raised in the Five Points neighborhood of Central El Paso and has dedicated his career to public service. A four-time graduate of UTEP, he previously served on the El Paso Independent School District Board of Trustees from 2019 to 2024 before being elected to the City Council.

officials.name: Jimmy Tran
officials.bio: Jimmy Tran was elected to serve as the Garland City Council Member for District 1 in May 2026. A Garland resident of over 24 years, Jimmy is deeply committed to strengthening the community through responsive leadership, public safety and sustainable economic growth.

officials.name: Joe Thomas Jr.
officials.bio: Joe Thomas Jr., District 7 Council Member, was elected to his first term on the Garland City Council in May 2025. He retired from full-time work in 2026 to devote more time to the city he loves. As a Council member, he aims to improve city infrastructure and continue Garland’s economic growth.

officials.name: Margaret Lucht
officials.bio: Margaret Lucht, District 5 City Council member, was sworn in for her first term in 2022. A lifelong resident of District 5, she is a Certified Dental Technician and currently a human resources administrator. She is dedicated to improving District 5 and making Garland a safer, more enjoyable place to live, work, and play.

officials.name: Carissa Dutton
officials.office: Deputy Mayor Pro Tem, City Council Member
officials.bio: Carissa Dutton, District 6 Council Member, was elected in May 2023. A 30-year resident of Garland, her extensive community service began as a teenager and includes tornado clean-up efforts, earning her Garland's first-ever Make Your Mark award in 2020. By profession a caretaker, she dedicates her free time to organizations like Garland Overnight Warming Station (GLOWS) and the Garland Optimist Club.

officials.name: Chris Ott
officials.office: Mayor Pro Tem, City Council Member
officials.bio: Chris Ott, District 8 Council Member, was elected to his first term in May 2023 and serves as Mayor Pro Tem. He is an advocate for the business community, open spaces, and the arts, with a history of civic involvement including 13 years on the City's Plan Commission. Chris is also a small business owner, having founded Rotary Performance in Garland in 1988.

officials.name: Dylan Hedrick
officials.bio: After serving three consecutive terms as District 7 Council member, Dylan Hedrick was elected to his first term as Garland Mayor in June of 2025. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering and a Masters of Business Administration from Rice University. As mayor, Dylan hopes to combine his engineering background with his business expertise to help rebuild city infrastructure, further Garland's economic development, and promote a better quality of life.

officials.bio: Will Jones moved to Waco in 1990, graduating from Baylor University with a B.B.A. in Finance, and had a successful career in the private sector before being elected County Commissioner for McLennan County, Precinct 3, in 2012. He is married to Merryl, has two sons, Grant and Reid, and is actively involved in his community and church.
